review_text: $349 is a lot for a watch that can't even show topo maps. Competitors give you more for less.
Pots are decent and the nonstick is fine so far. I've only used it for four trips though, so can't say how it ages.
Great light, but I can't switch between red and white mode without cycling through every setting. Every. Single. Time.
Lights with one click and the flame control is smooth. Sets up in about ten seconds even with gloves on.
Ordered Monday night, on my porch Wednesday morning. Packaging was tight and nothing was dented.
Fabric feels thinner than my old tent but it kept out one light shower. I'll update after a real storm.
Plenty of pockets, though I'm still figuring out where everything goes. The rain cover is easy to find.
Stitching is holding up great after a 12-day trek through the Cascades. Zero fraying, zippers still smooth. Worth every penny.
Arrived on the estimated date, box a little beat up but the poles were fine. Nothing to complain about, nothing to rave about.
Broke these in over one weekend with no blisters, and they stayed dry through an ankle-deep creek crossing. Shipping took forever but who cares, the boots are fantastic.
Screen scratched within two weeks and the strap is already peeling. Battery life is fine but it looks like it's been through a war.
The carrier left it at the wrong building and it took me a week to track it down. Bottle looks fine though.
The igniter died on the third use and the pot supports feel flimsy. Nice to know I can still light it with a lighter like it's 1995.
Chat agent was friendly but kept pointing me to the FAQ page. I ended up solving it myself.
Shipped fast and the tracking link actually worked. Haven't had it out in the cold yet, so no word on the bag itself.
Hood adjustment is a mess. Toggles are tiny and the cord tangles every time I stuff it back in the pocket.
Ice was still in there after 30 hours. The powder coat has survived my truck bed without a single chip.
Didn't expect much at this level but it held up through a full day of Pacific Northwest drizzle. Taped seams are solid so far.
Waited 11 days for a reply about my broken clip. When someone finally answered, it was a copy-paste response that ignored my question.
Simple once you read the manual. The wind guard is a bit fiddly to attach but I got it.
The strap adjuster is impossible to use with gloves on, and the app needs three taps just to start a hike. Why is this so hard?
Lost a fistful of down in the first week and the shoulder seam is already leaking feathers. It's pricey too, but the leaking is what really bugs me.
Lid arrived cracked, so I messaged support and they sent a new one the same day. No photos, no hassle.
Slept at 18 degrees in the Smokies and was toasty all night. The down loft is impressive for the weight.
Boots were a half size too small and the support team set up an exchange in one email. Replacement arrived in three days.
One pole bent at the lower section the first time it wedged between rocks. I expected a little flex, not a fold.
Support was polite and answered within a day, but couldn't fix my syncing problem. They offered a refund instead, which I'll take.
Getting in and out of this thing is a wrestling match. The zipper snags the draft tube every time and the pull tab is too small to find in the dark.
Nice jacket I guess, but $279 feels steep. You can find the same fill power for under $200 elsewhere.
Called the warranty line three times and got disconnected twice. Still no resolution on my torn rain fly.
Caught it during the 25% off sale and it felt like stealing. I'd have paid full price, honestly, but the discount was a no-brainer.
Priced about the same as the other insulated bottles I looked at. Neither a bargain nor overpriced.
Standard shipping took six days, which is what the site said. It's fine.
Compared with the big-name sets at double the price this does the same job. Great deal.
Delivery was supposed to be Thursday and it showed up the following Wednesday. I needed it for a weekend trip and missed it.
They cost more than I wanted to spend, but you do get what you pay for. Not cheap, not a rip-off either.
The hip belt adjusts easily and the side pocket is reachable without taking the pack off. Little things add up on a long day.
Package sat at a distribution center for nine days with no updates. When it finally came the box was soaked.
Wow, only four emails to get someone to actually read my message. Impressive service from Northwind. The tent poles are still broken, by the way.
For $29 this is absurd value. Bright beam, runs all night, and I bought a second one for my brother.
